full_text:
Since the adoption of United Nations Security Council Resolution 2286 in 2016 and 09 June 2026, Insecurity Insight has documented over 
19,000
 attacks on health care worldwide, highlighting the persistent and widespread failure to protect health care in conflict.

To mark a decade since the adoption, Insecurity Insight released a landmark report analysing ten years of violence against health care. Drawing on a decade of systematically collected data, 
Still Under Attack
 documents the scale, patterns, and consequences of attacks on health care in conflict-affected settings around the world. Among the report's key findings:

More than 3,860 health workers were killed and over 2,500 were arrested or detained between January 2016 and December 2025.

Local health workers remain particularly vulnerable, accounting for more than 65% of documented health worker killings.

The growing use of armed drones and explosive weapons is contributing to increasing damage to health facilities and to health worker deaths and injuries.

Based exclusively on Insecurity Insight's data collection, the report shows how violence against health care has become increasingly normalised, with severe consequences for civilians, disease response, and the resilience of health systems. The report also provides detailed analysis of perpetrators, methods of attack, and emerging risks, including the growing role of new technologies in conflict. It concludes with recommendations for governments, international organisations, humanitarian actors, and the diplomatic community to strengthen the protection of health care and improve accountability for violations.

Africa
Democratic Republic of the Congo
13 June 2026:
 In Watsa territory, Haut-Uele province, the head nurse at Mungbere General Referral Hospital was shot and killed by a soldier who was reportedly attempting to speak to a patient receiving treatment, and the nurse was shot while intervening to inquire about the situation and protect the patient. 
Source:
 
Radio Okapi

As reported on 14 June 2026:
 In Mongbwalu town, Djugu territory, Ituri province, health workers burying a suspected Ebola casualty were violently obstructed from accessing a coffin by residents. Police officers warned residents not to touch the coffin but were later forced to use warning shots and tear gas to allow health workers to retrieve the body. 
Source: Personal Communication

15 June 2026:
 In Wanamahika Mutiri area, Butembo city, North Kivu province, Adventist (Wanamahika) Hospital was stormed by unidentified armed men carrying bladed weapons and knives, who abducted a woman and her six-year-old daughter from the facility. The child had tested positive for Ebola. The mother and daughter were later found at an Ebola treatment centre roughly 18km from Butembo. 
Sources:
 
Actualite,
 
AOL,
 
BBC
 
and
 
Reuters

16 June 2026:
 In Ituri province, five Ebola response workers were briefly kidnapped by armed groups. 
Sources:
 
Namibia Daily News
 
and
 
United Nations

16 June 2026:
 In Kakumba village, Walungu territory, South Kivu province, two Red Cross workers wearing Red Cross emblems were killed by armed men while on a mission to supervise drinking water supply work. The armed men allegedly knew the nature of their mission in the area. 
Sources:
 
ICRC
 
and
 
Radio Okapi

Insecurity Insight’s latest social media monitoring brief analyses public narratives surrounding the 17th Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo between 15 June to 22 June 2026. 
Key findings:

Politics, not the outbreak, drove the conversation. Comment volume rose 33% on the previous period, but almost entirely on the back of a single statement by an opposition figure linking the DRC's World Cup performance to governance failures (1,160 comments, 26.5% of the total). Harmful content stayed minimal in posts and scattered in comments.

A government attempt to deflect criticism onto an NGO backfired. After a health organisation warned of "dangerous gaps" in the response, the government rejected the criticism as "alarmist" and urged NGOs to show restraint. The backlash was overwhelmingly hostile to the government rather than the NGO, and dominated by the "Ebola business" corruption frame.

A cluster of attacks on Ebola facilities and health workers was amplified and reframed online. The incidents are real and corroborated, but their online life was driven by a small network of accounts - and the single highest-reach post had over 400,000 views.

Data from Insecurity Insight shows that since 21 May and 21 June 2026, at least 
19 incidents
 of violence against or obstruction of health care impacting Ebola response measures were reported. Two Ebola treatment facilities were attacked and deliberately set on fire and another vandalised, damaging windows and a water supply system, compromising access to drinking water. Health workers were repeatedly assaulted, threatened and violently obstructed from performing their duties.

211 health workers were killed, 15 kidnapped and 127 arrested

Health facilities were damaged 216 times

affected health care

Asia
Pakistan
Between 05 June - 01 July 2026:
 In Quetta city, Balochistan province, a female doctor was attacked and severely burned with acid inside the Civil Hospital by a hospital lift operator. A medical technician was also burned when he rushed to help the doctor. The lift operator was later shot and killed by police who tracked him down at a local bus station. In response to the acid attack, doctors staged protests in Quetta. 
Sources:
 
Arab News,
 
Ians Live
 
and
 
The Jerusalem Post

Myanmar

Data collected by Insecurity Insight shows that since the military coup on 01 February 2021 and 04 June 2026 at least 
1,943 incidents
 of violence against or obstruction of access to health care took place across Myanmar:

equivalent to one attack on health care every day for more than five years

65% of these attacks were attributed to the Myanmar Armed Forces (MAF)

175 health workers were killed and 932 arrested

health facilities were damaged on at least 509 occasions

So far this year, at least seven health workers were killed by explosive weapons. Five health workers were killed in three incidents involving MAF airstrikes: two occurred at prisoner-of-war detention facilities under the control of opposition forces in Rakhine and Yangon, while the third involved the bombing of a hospital located in areas under the control of the PDF in Sagaing. A further two health workers were killed in two separate roadside landmine explosions reportedly attributed to opposition forces in Bago and Magway regions.

Insecurity Insight has documented over 
3,000 attacks
 on Ukraine’s health facilities, health workers and infrastructure since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion on 24 February 2022 to 30 April 2026, averaging nearly two attacks per day.

Hospitals and clinics have been damaged or destroyed 1,632 times

462 health workers have been killed and 476 others injured.

113 attacks on services provided for women during pregnancy, childbirth and the postnatal period

 In Tyre city and district, South governorate, MSF temporarily suspended activities, including its mobile clinics and support to Jabal Amel Hospital, Qana Hospital and the Lebanese-Italian Hospital, following large-scale evacuation orders issued by the Israeli army covering Tyre, its camps and several surrounding areas. MSF evacuated its teams to Sidon and stated that the suspension was due to the forced displacement of residents and the deteriorating security situation.

 In Tyre district, South governorate, the vicinity of Hiram Hospital was hit by an Israeli airstrike, injuring 10 nurses and hospital staff members. Patient rooms and the emergency department were damaged, and windows were shattered in staff vehicles.

and

 In Sidon city, Tyre district, South governorate, a pregnant nurse was killed in an Israeli airstrike.

Occupied Palestinian territory

Data collected by Insecurity Insight shows that between 07 October 2023 and 09 June 2026, at least 3,327 incidents of violence against or obstruction of access to health care took place across the occupied Palestinian territory. 95% of all incidents were attributed to Israeli forces.

Gaza:
 2,328 attacks on health care were recorded during which health facilities were damaged 448 times, 765 health workers were killed and 398 arrested. Patient access to medicine was obstructed on 289 occasions.

West Bank and East Jerusalem:
 938 attacks on health care were recorded during which health facilities were damaged 30 times, 12 health workers were killed and 188 arrested. Patient access to medicine was obstructed on 579 occasions.

Of the 938 attacks on health care in the West Bank, 47 were attributed to Israeli settlers, who were typically armed with guns or rocks. The proportion of such attacks more than doubled in 
2025
 compared to 2024, rising from around 2% to 9% of total reported attacks. Between 01 January and 09 June 2026, Israeli settler-attributed attacks increased further, accounting for 22% of all reported attacks during that period. Most Israeli settler attacks on health care targeted ambulances and first responders, including blocking their access to those needing care. On at least seven occasions, Israeli settlers attacked health care under the protection of the IDF.

 In Ar Raqqa city and governorate, the vicinity of the National Hospital and Intifada School was under threat when the Interior Ministry was attacked in a suicide bombing by unidentified perpetrators, killing two employees of the Interior Ministry. 11 June 2026:
 In Al-Darain area, Sheikh Othman district, Aden city, two doctors who were husband and wife, both employed at Doctors' Tower Hospital, were shot and killed alongside two Yemeni soldiers, and an unspecified number of others were wounded, when a soldier guarding the home of the governor of Yemen opened fire in the morning. The soldier was later killed during an attempted arrest by security forces.

The Americas
Colombia
18 June 2026:
 In García Herreros neighbourhood, Cúcuta city, Norte de Santander department, a pharmacy was robbed and an employee threatened and hit by two men armed with pistols. Cash was stolen from the register. 
Source:
 
Cucuta Online

Haiti
18-19 April 2026:
 In Port-au-Prince city and arrondissement, MSF staff members were trapped in their homes during clashes between rival armed groups with intense gunfire. Nearly 40 people, including the MSF staff and their families, sought refuge in the MSF hospital in Cité Soleil, having no other safe option. 
Source:
 
MSF

15 June 2026:
 In Cité Soleil, Port-au-Prince city and arrondissement, the MSF-supported Isaïe Jeanty Maternity Hospital was hit and damaged by numerous stray bullets amid crossfire between armed groups. A woman was injured in the leg by a stray bullet inside the hospital grounds. MSF suspended activities the next morning but continued to provide emergency care, patients’ stabilisation and referrals for several days. On 19 June, the organisation evacuated its staff and suspended all activities. 
Source:
 
MSF

Other resources

Attacks on health care were relentless in 2025. Using data collected by Insecurity Insight, the Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition (SHCC) recorded 
2,546 incidents in 33 countries
 in which damage to or the destruction of health care facilities was reported on at least 790 occasions, 455 health workers were killed, 218 kidnapped and 263 arrested.

Key findings in 2025

Violence rose in 13 countries and recorded incidents remained far above the ten-year annual average.

Continued high levels of violence by state forces alongside rising levels of violence by non-state armed actors.

The expansion of remotely piloted aerial systems (drones) increasingly affected health care in conflict settings.

Kidnapping of health workers increased, particularly in the Central African Republic, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mali, Pakistan and Syria.
